subject: Capacity pilot tech walk recap & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@avatech.io>, Marcus Chen <marcus@avatech.io>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity pilot tech walk recap & next steps

Hi Sara / Marcus —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through Avatech's inference needs. Quick recap from my side so we’re aligned and we can move toward a concrete pilot: 

Primary pain points you called out:
- Unpredictable token costs and long tail latency during customer peaks (p95 spikes to ~600–800ms).
- Multi-tenant interference on your current cluster — you want strict isolation for production models.
- Autoscaling has been reactive; need predictable burst behavior without manual intervention.

Current stack notes you shared:
- Self-hosted Kubernetes cluster running Triton for some models and a custom Flask API for orchestration.
- Mix of consumer GPUs and older A100 cards; some models are quantized, others run FP16.
- Traffic profile: steady 250–350 TPS during business hours, occasional spikes to ~700 TPS for short bursts.

Success criteria for a pilot (what would make this a success for Avatech):
- Stable p95 latency under 200ms for your 90% of requests at target throughput.
- Predictable throughput at committed capacity (no more than ~5–10% variance).
- Isolation guarantees for model data + logs, and an operational path to scale to full production within 6–8 weeks.
- Demonstrated unit-cost improvement or clear cost predictability compared to current ops.

Proposed next steps (I’ll follow up with a calendar invite after you confirm):
1) Share traffic/latency samples (you mentioned a CSV dump) — please send those (sensitive fields redacted).
2) Technical deep-dive with Marissa (SE) to validate pilot config and region (you asked for us-west2).
3) Proposed pilot configuration: reserved pool equivalent to 4x H100 (or 8x A100-80GB), with autoscale headroom of +2 GPUs for short bursts; 6-week pilot window including load testing.
4) Security/compliance touchpoint: we’ll provide SOC2 scope and a short MSA outline for review.

Attachments: avatech-pilot-outline-v1.pdf (pilot overview), pilot-config.yaml (initial config stub)

If that matches your notes, I’ll loop Marissa & Connor into the technical kick-off and propose times for the deep-dive.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
calendly.com/jordan-redwood

Thanks for the context — happy to lead the technical deep-dive. A few quick items I’ll bring to the call and follow up with docs: 

1) Proposed pilot footprint (initial):
   - 4x H100 (reserved pool) as baseline for steady 300 TPS at your median payload.
   - Autoscale policy: burst headroom +2 H100 nodes for up-to-10min bursts (policy based on queue length + CPU/KV cache hit).
   - If H100 unavailable, equivalent: 8x A100-80GB with sharded routing.

2) Load test plan:
   - Synthetic load replay using your latency CSV + a synthetic fan-out pattern to replicate 10–15 minute spikes.
   - Validation metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rates.

3) Ops details to confirm during call:
   - Region: US-West2 (you confirmed).
   - Networking: VPC peering or private link? They indicated private tenancy so we’ll prepare VPC options.
   - Data residency & logs: we’ll scope minimal retention for pilot and add extended retention as an add-on.

I’ll attach a short pilot runbook after the call and a first-pass pilot-config.yaml so procurement has numbers. Connor — if you can draft the MAM milestones (kickoff, load test, review, go/no-go) I’ll drop durations.

Available for the deep-dive Tue 10:30am PT — Jordan, please send calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
